title: Smoothed cost model for granular kernel choreography
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We observe per-request kernel choice oscillation on heterogeneous GPUs for mixed sequence-length workloads. Short bursts of traffic cause noisy cost estimates, which leads the current selector to flip kernels during a single user session and worsen tail latency. We need a lightweight, robust cost model that (1) smooths short-term noise, (2) respects sequence-length buckets and architecture capabilities, and (3) provides a low-overhead exploration schedule for discovering better kernels without regressing latency SLOs.

Proposal summary: Implement a smoothed cost model + exploration policy called Smoothed Kernel Choreography (SKC). SKC combines exponentially weighted moving averages (EWMA) of latency/cost per (arch, seqlen-bucket, op-mode) cell with a leaky upper-confidence bonus for controlled exploration. Key ideas: 1) Maintain per-cell EWMA for latency and token-cost with decay tuned for request rate. 2) Bucket sequence lengths into asymmetric buckets (0-32,33-64,65-128,129-512,>512) derived from our production histograms. 3) Use a bandit-derived exploration budget at the request-path level: allow up to X% of requests per minute to probe candidates prioritized by estimated upside / regression risk. 4) Probe policy uses micro-probing for prefill paths (short warmups) and full-run probes for decode-heavy paths. 5) Integrate a confidence threshold so high-SLO requests can pin to stable kernels while background traffic can explore.

Attention heuristics and optimizations: Add a detection layer for compatibility with fast attention kernels (e.g., FlashAttention variants) that tags model variants by attention arithmetic pattern during model ingestion. The runtime will maintain candidate kernel families (default, flash-optimized, sparse-attn-friendly) and only consider probes within families compatible with model ops. For sequences where KV cache reuse is high, prefer kernels with faster KV read performance even if raw decode microbenchmarks are slightly slower.

Prefill/Decode scheduling changes: Prefill paths will carry a lightweight request annotation specifying expected decode length percentile (p50/p95). SKC uses this to decide between prefilling on a single optimized kernel vs a hybrid prefill+decode split (prefill on stable kernel, decode on low-latency candidate). Implement a prefetch budget to keep warm KV around for hot sessions (L1 cache TTL per-session).

Success metrics (measured in Console):
- 99th percentile latency change (prefill and decode) <= +5ms compared to baseline for production traffic.
- Mean token-cost reduction >= 4% on mixed workloads after 2 weeks of exploration.
- Probe-induced error rate < 0.05% and probe traffic adheres to exploration budget.

Rollout plan:
1) Lab spike: microbenchmarks across GPU types + synthetic traffic with seqlen mix (2 weeks).
2) Canary: 1% of production requests, observability hooks for per-cell EWMA, probe counts, fallback events (2 weeks).
3) Gradual ramp to 20% with automated rollback if 99p latency or error budget exceeded (4 weeks).

Implementation outline / tasks:
- Spike: implement per-cell EWMA store and offline analyzer to pick decay params (Ava) (3d).
- Runtime: add SKC selector module with probe quota enforcement and per-request annotation plumbing (Ravi) (2w).
- Ingestion: tag model artifacts with attention-family metadata during model onboarding (Model Onboarding team) (4d).
- Observability: Console panels for latency by (arch,seqlen-bucket,kernel), probe rate, probe failures, probe rollbacks (Data & Console) (1w).
- Tests: end-to-end tests for probe budget, rollback, and pinned requests. Load tests with mixed seqlen distribution.

Risks & mitigations:
- Over-exploration causing latency regressions: mitigate with conservative probe budget and immediate rollback threshold on 99p latency.
- Model mis-tagging for attention family: add validation test during onboarding and fallback to conservative family.
- Storage overhead for per-cell metrics: aggregate to time-series rollups with retention windows and sparse sharding by active cells.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for EWMA, probe budget enforcement, and fallback logic pass in CI.
- Canary shows no >5ms 99p latency regression and probe failures <0.05%.
- Console panels show expected per-cell convergence over time and allow filtering by region/hardware.

Documentation & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/SKC+Design 
- Lab spike notebook (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/SKC-spike 
- Spike microbench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2637

Notes: This approach intentionally biases toward stability while allowing bounded exploration. It complements (rather than replaces) heavier offline autotuners that run long-running calibration jobs.
